clue.text: Bald male by bar: 'Like some drugs?'

parts.note: a bald statement is plain and undisguised, that is, overt
he is the male pronoun
a bar in a pub is the counter

explanation.surface: A bald man sits by the bar and someone asks about the medicines he takes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just puts the pieces side by side. 'Bald' looks like hairlessness but here means blunt or open.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicines sold without a prescription are sold across the shop's serving surface, so the phrase describes non-prescription drugs.

clue.text: Men come down over a city in Florida

parts.note: OR is other ranks, enlisted men
to come down from the air is to land
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Soldiers fly in and land at a Florida city.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme-park city in central Florida, home of Walt Disney World, is a well-known example.

clue.text: Certain need to broadcast the French agreement

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Some French accord must certainly be announced.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1904 friendly understanding between Britain and France is the classic example of a diplomatic agreement.

clue.text: Ancient city, partly destroyed

indicators.note: partly means only part of the word destroyed is used

explanation.surface: An old city was partly ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: The city besieged by the Greeks in Homer's Iliad is a classic example of an ancient city.

clue.text: Woman, English, upper-class, and refined

parts.note: U denotes upper-class usage
nice can mean fine, subtle or refined

explanation.surface: Describes a woman who is English, upper-class and genteel.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Elderly take pride in flag

parts.note: elderly means old
to glory in something is to take pride in it

explanation.surface: Old people are proud of their national banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname for the Stars and Stripes, the United States national banner.

clue.text: Current landlord's brought round second bulletin

indicators.note: brought round means the second letter is placed ahead of the landlord

parts.note: current means new, up to date
a landlord lets property, so is a letter

explanation.surface: The present landlord has delivered a second notice.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter here is one who lets, not something posted.
explanation.definitionFit: A periodical printed circular sent to members is a type of bulletin.

clue.text: Conservationists in Liege hear things to be rebuilt

indicators.note: to be rebuilt means the letters must be reconstructed in a new order

explanation.surface: Preservationists in the Belgian city of Liege learn of buildings to be restored.
explanation.walkthrough: English Heritage is the body that looks after historic sites in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The organisation caring for Stonehenge and other historic English monuments is a group of conservationists.

clue.text: Toast for model

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
to model for an artist is to sit

explanation.surface: A drinking salute offered on behalf of a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A German and Latin salutation said when raising glasses, meaning may it benefit you, is a toast.

clue.text: Lease, in writing, causes disappointment

parts.note: to lease a property is to let it
something put down is recorded in writing

explanation.surface: A tenancy agreement on paper turns out to be a disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticlimax that fails to meet expectations is a familiar synonym for a disappointment.

clue.text: Lady whose husband's gone in punt after party

indicators.note: after means the bet word comes following the party word

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
a punt is a bet, a wager

explanation.surface: A woman who has lost her husband spends time on a boat after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests a flat-bottomed boat, but it is a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: A widow holding a title or property from her late spouse is called by this name.

clue.text: Improper noun, not socially acceptable

indicators.note: improper means not proper or in correct order, so the letters of noun are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammarian complains that a noun is used improperly and unfit for polite company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Improper noun' reads like grammar talk, the opposite of a proper noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Coined in the 1950s for speech or habits not typical of the upper class, so socially unacceptable.

clue.text: One sheepdog's devouring the Spanish confections

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: devouring means the sheepdogs swallow the Spanish article inside them

parts.note: collies are sheepdogs, read here in the plural
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A sheepdog is gobbling up some Spanish sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheepdog's' is read as a plural noun, not a possessive. 'devouring' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen flavoured treats on a stick are sweet confections, the British name for popsicles.

clue.text: Enterprise, outfit with work

parts.note: a getup is an outfit of clothes
and means together with
a machine that goes is working

explanation.surface: Showing initiative by wearing the right clothes to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy and initiative, the drive to get things done, is the sense of enterprise meant.

clue.text: First of a series of games is key

definitions.text: First of a series of games
definitions.meaning: the first match of a series is the opening one
a key is a device that opens a lock

explanation.surface: The first match of a series is crucial.
explanation.definitionFit: The first match is the series' starting game, and a key is a tool that unlocks things.

clue.text: Short bad-tempered note

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back, losing its final letter

parts.note: crotchety means irritable and bad-tempered

explanation.surface: Someone writes a curt, cross message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' and 'note' suggest a brief message; 'Short' trims CROTCHETY of its last letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter note in music, lasting one beat in common time, is the British name for this musical note.

clue.text: Drama in gym — gentry involved

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of gentry are twisted

explanation.surface: Members of the upper class get caught up in a fuss at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drama' suggests a commotion; it is Ibsen's verse play.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen's 1867 verse play about a Norwegian wanderer is a celebrated drama.

clue.text: Sang together making record about solar god, Eastern

indicators.note: about means the record wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: CD is a compact disc, a record
Horus is the Egyptian falcon-headed god associated with the sun

explanation.surface: A choir records a hymn about an Egyptian sun god.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing in unison as a group is to perform as a choir, the verb sense of chorus.

clue.text: Painter like Picasso, bachelor, lives in style

indicators.note: in means the bachelor and lives pieces sit inside the style word

parts.note: the cut of a garment is its style
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: A single artist living stylishly, in the manner of Picasso.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso co-founded the movement of geometric fragmented forms, so a painter of that school is like him.

clue.text: Level pegging on board in game

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, so the ship letters wrap the level word

parts.note: board here evokes a vessel, and SS is a steamship
level pegging means scores are even

explanation.surface: Two players are neck and neck in a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a crossword convention for going inside SS, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby played with seven-a-side teams is a well-known game, as in the Hong Kong tournament.

clue.text: Withdraw claw

definitions.meaning: to pull out of a race or contest is to withdraw
to rake with nails or talons is to claw

explanation.surface: Retract a cat's talon.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant pulled from a race is struck off the list, and raking with nails is clawing.

clue.text: False report in article penned by witty type

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed, as in a pen, by the witty type

parts.note: a card is a joker, a witty person
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A humorist writes a piece containing a hoax.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumour or hoax story that is untrue is a canard, from the French word for duck.

clue.text: Time when nothing goes right in musical put on outside during recess

indicators.note: during means the inner group sits within the recess word

parts.note: a bay is a recess in a wall or coastline

indicators.note: outside means the put-on word goes around the musical

parts.note: to put on is to add
Hair is the 1960s rock musical

explanation.surface: A musical is staged outdoors in the school holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' looks like a break or holiday but means an alcove here. 'outside' and 'during' are two nested containment signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a day of frustration when everything seems to go wrong, as if one's grooming had failed.

clue.text: Row right after game in Cup

indicators.note: after means the right letter follows the game

parts.note: a cup tie is a knockout match in a cup competition

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out after a cup match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' can rhyme with 'cow' (a quarrel) but here means a line, as of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer or line of seats rising above another is a synonym for a row.

clue.text: Fish caught on a river trip, finally

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: finally means take the final letter of trip

explanation.surface: An angler finally lands a fish on a river outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish of the minnow family, popular with anglers, is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Support partnership, extremely busy

parts.note: in cricket a stand is a partnership between two batters

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters, first and last, of busy

explanation.surface: A busy pair back each other up.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a stand is runs scored together by two batters at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve kept ready in case of need is a backup, a form of support.

clue.text: Resolute, a worker crossing weir

indicators.note: crossing means the a and worker pieces span across the weir, holding it between them

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
a dam is a barrier like a weir

explanation.surface: A determined labourer walks over a weir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' looks like walking over, but here the first two pieces straddle the weir, one on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unshakeably firm in purpose is determined, a near synonym of resolute.

clue.text: In prep, he sorted out English chapter giving a grammatical term

indicators.note: in means the English chapter letters go inside the rearranged group
out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: During homework, a pupil sorts out an English chapter on grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder, with 'out' the indicator; EC goes into the anagram of PREPHESORTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Indirect speech, relaying what someone said without quoting them, is a standard grammatical term.
